This binding likely disrupts the normal function of DNA polymerase eta, potentially leading to impaired DNA synthesis and cell cycle arrest. The evidence suggests that chloroquine's effect on DNA polymerase eta is mediated through its interaction with ECC10, highlighting a critical role in the pathophysiology of the disease.
